images.title: How far in one hour
images.purpose: Show the eight distances a person can generally travel in one hour, one per means of travel, with the distance as the largest text.
images.composition: A header line at the top and a board of 8 cards in 2 columns of 4, each with a small picture, the means of travel and the distance in large type.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas. TOP: one header line, In one hour a person can generally travel. BELOW: a board of exactly 8 rounded cards in 2 columns of 4 rows, thin dark outlines, white fill. In each card a small flat picture sits at the left, the means of travel in small dark text at the top right, and under it the distance in very large bold teal #0072B2 type. LEFT COLUMN, top to bottom: (1) a walking person, on foot, 3 to 5 km; (2) a person on a horse, on horseback, 10 to 15 km; (3) a bicycle, by cycle, 12 to 20 km; (4) a motorbike, by motorbike, 40 to 60 km. RIGHT COLUMN, top to bottom: (5) a train, by train, 40 to 160 km; (6) a ship, by ship, 25 to 45 km; (7) an aeroplane, by aircraft, 750 to 920 km; (8) a spacecraft, by spacecraft, at least 28,000 km. In each distance the numbers are the largest element and km is smaller. No other numbers, no arrows, no scale.
labels: In one hour a person can generally travel
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The distance covered in one hour depends on how we travel, from a 1-digit number of kilometres on foot to a 5-digit number by spacecraft.
images.description: A board of the eight distances a person can generally travel in one hour: on foot, on horseback, by cycle, by motorbike, by train, by ship, by aircraft and by spacecraft.
images.context: Starting point is the chapter's own list of what a person can generally travel in an hour. The eight distances are exactly the book's and nothing is added. The book's wording for the spacecraft is minimum 28,000 km; the picture says at least 28,000 km, which means the same.
images.teaching_notes: Read the board together and count the digits of the smallest and the largest number: 3 has 1 digit, 28,000 has 5. Do not add a speed or any other distance to this picture.

image_decisions.why: The board of the book's eight distances is the whole content of the concept and reads best as one picture.
